title: 0.14.0: lore check reports an ADR status outside the profile enum, and lore supersede sets both ends
description: Operator-approved 0.14.0 item (opum-doc seq 179, ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-10, read verbatim on opum-agent OPAG-1094 at origin/dev 647473bd): (a) lore check reports an ADR whose status is outside the profile enum, and lore supersede sets both ends. Design of record: opum-doc docs/reference/questions-decisions-and-adrs.md. Workers implement exactly this and report issues to opum-doc; they make no design calls. Filed 2026-10-03, not to be started until the 0.13.0 PR (opum-ai/lore-cli#476) is merged and the fleet restart is behind us.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore check enforces the ADR status enum (draft, stable, deprecated) on every OKF version: an out-of-enum status is an error on 0.1 AND on 0.2, and all three valid values pass on both.
lore supersede writes deprecated (not the invalid superseded) on a 0.1 bundle, setting both ends.
The CHANGELOG names the one-line fix for existing 0.1 ADRs that carry status: superseded.

implementationNotes:
INVESTIGATION (2026-10-14, branch feat/LCLI-669-adr-status-enum-and-supersede-ends). Design of record read BY REF: opum-doc docs/reference/questions-decisions-and-adrs.md, section "Lore, built by lore-cli in 0.14.0".
(a) AC2 IS ALREADY DONE and tested: src/commands/supersede.ts wires superseded_by plus the lifecycle marker on the old concept and supersedes on the new one, and test/supersede.test.ts asserts status: deprecated (OKF 0.2) and status: superseded (legacy OKF 0.1). Nothing to implement.
(b) AC1 exists ONLY for OKF 0.2 bundles: src/core/schema.ts validateVersionedFrontmatter returns early unless profile.okfVersion === "0.2", and lore-cli's OWN bundle is OKF 0.1 (docs/index.md carries no okf_version), so an out-of-enum ADR status is silently accepted here. PROVED by probe: an ADR carrying status: superseded in this bundle produced a frontmatter warning for a missing summary and required-section errors, but NO finding for the status itself. No test anywhere asserts the lifecycle-status rejection.
(c) CONFLICT needing a ruling: lore supersede deliberately writes the LEGACY status: superseded on the old ADR in a 0.1 bundle, so a version-independent ADR status check would flag lore supersede's own output. The design of record says the old ADR goes to deprecated (a profile value), so either supersede should stop writing superseded in 0.1, or the check must be scoped. The task says workers make no design calls, so this is REPORTED, not settled.

DEC-192 (opum-ai/opum-doc#1004), relayed by the leader 2026-10-14, verbatim in substance: option A, task UNPARKED, ordinary under DEC-182. Both bundles' adr.schema.json define the status enum as [draft, stable, deprecated] (opum-doc read at 03:19Z), so "superseded" was never valid in 0.1 — this is a DEFECT FIX, not a behaviour change. supersede writes "deprecated" on 0.1, and check enforces the enum on every OKF version. Prove it both ways: out-of-enum is an error on 0.1 AND 0.2, and the three valid values pass on both. The CHANGELOG names the one-line fix for existing 0.1 ADRs. Branch feat/LCLI-669-adr-status-enum-and-supersede-ends; one branch, one PR; stop at the green head for a DEC-183 reviewer; do not merge.

DEC-192 AMENDED in opum-ai/opum-doc#1006 (relayed by the leader, 2026-10-14): the phrase "every OKF version" meant VERSIONS, not types. The lifecycle enum is enforced on ADR documents on both 0.1 and 0.2; the 0.1 task-rollup `status` on task-coupled types is untouched, because there `status` IS the rollup key (check.ts:16/:804) with the todo/in-progress/done vocabulary. Decided A out of the 38 -> 9 finding.

CLASS 2 IS THE INTENDED OUTCOME (leader, 2026-10-14): a legacy ADR carrying `status: superseded` is invalid, so exit 6 (validation) answers before the already-superseded guard. Done: line 80 and the router assertions now expect `deprecated`; the 8 fixtures moved to the valid already-superseded shape (`status: deprecated` + `superseded_by`), each still answering conflict/exit 5; a new test pins that a legacy `status: superseded` ADR makes supersede exit 6 with the invalid value named; and the guard's SUPERSEDED_STATUS arm was REMOVED as unreachable rather than left as dead code.

THIS BUNDLE'S OWN FIX: `lore check` caught two of lore-cli's own ADRs carrying the legacy marker -- docs/adr/0009-story-task-coupling-reconciliation.md and docs/adr/0015-lightweight-retrieval-no-vectors.md -- and both were moved `status: superseded` -> `status: deprecated` (the CHANGELOG's one-line fix), with their `superseded_by` untouched. lore check is green.

RECORD CORRECTION (LCLI-669 review F1, applied 2026-10-14). The CLASS-2 note above and the final summary both said the already-superseded guard's `status: superseded` arm "was removed". That is FALSE as of round 2 and is corrected here rather than deleted, so the record shows both the claim and its correction.

The arm is PRESENT and LIVE: src/commands/supersede.ts's assertNotAlreadySuperseded (:327) refuses when hasRecordedSuccessor OR statusIsSuperseded (:353). It was removed in the first revision and RESTORED in 000df7c1, because review F4 showed it reachable — a 0.1 NON-ADR (a Story, a Reference) keeps `status` as its task-rollup key under the carve-out, so such a document LOADS with the legacy marker, and without the arm wireOld would clobber its rollup `status` to `deprecated`.

What round 1 got wrong was not the removal but the CLAIM THAT THE ARM WAS UNREACHABLE. Supersede's own module header, the guard docstring and the hint were corrected with it, and a test covers the live path.
finalSummary: Delivered as opum-ai/lore-cli#579 (merged 08414ef9). DEC-192 half 1: `lore supersede` writes `deprecated` on a 0.1 bundle, not the never-valid `superseded`. Half 2, DEC-192 as amended in opum-ai/opum-doc#1006: the lifecycle enum is enforced on ADR documents on BOTH OKF versions, and only there on 0.1 -- on 0.1 the same `status` field is the task-rollup key for task-coupled types (check.ts:16/:804), whose vocabulary is todo/in-progress/done, so the broad reading broke 38 tests and the LORE-27 drift surface. Proved both ways on 0.1 and 0.2 in test/lifecycle-status-enum.test.ts, plus the 0.1 Story rollup carve-out. CORRECTED (review F1): the already-superseded guard RETAINS its `status: superseded` arm -- review F4 showed it reachable on a 0.1 NON-ADR, where the marker loads under the carve-out -- and it refuses such a target as a conflict instead of clobbering its rollup status; a legacy `status: superseded` ADR, which cannot load, exits 6 with the invalid value named. `lore check` caught this bundle's own ADR-0009 and ADR-0015 carrying the legacy marker; both take the CHANGELOG's one-line fix. Verified locally: `lore check` 0 errors on the MERGED state, typecheck and lint clean, full suite green.
